t: You're standing where Devonshire House once stood on Piccadilly. It was the London townhouse of the Dukes of Devonshire. After a fire in 1733 it was rebuilt in the Palladian style to designs by William Kent, and finished around 1740. It stood empty after the First World War and was demolished in 1924. Georgiana, Duchess of Devonshire, the Whig organiser, writer and style icon, died here in 1806. Her daughter, also named Georgiana, was born here in 1783 and later became Countess of Carlisle.
